articles.title: Dual-Mode Propulsion: MIT's Game-Changing Engine Could Unleash Small Satellites on the Solar System
articles.summary: MIT engineers have created a propulsion system that lets a spacecraft use one fuel for both high-thrust chemical burns and efficient electric propulsion. This breakthrough could give tiny satellites the flexibility to journey to Mars, the asteroid belt, and beyond, dramatically expanding what small, low-cost missions can achieve.

articles.title: A Complete Fly Connectome Reveals a Surprising Twist: The Body Calls the Shots
articles.summary: Scientists have published the first complete wiring diagram of an adult fruit fly's central nervous system, linking the brain and nerve cord. The connectome reveals that many behaviors are driven by local circuits in the body, not a central brain command, upending assumptions about how nervous systems coordinate action.

articles.title: The Stroop Test Exposes a Critical Flaw in AI: It Can't Ignore Distractions Like Humans Do
articles.summary: When researchers gave leading AI models the classic Stroop task—naming ink colors while ignoring conflicting words—performance collapsed as lists grew longer. The systems defaulted to reading words, revealing a fundamental lack of executive control that sets human attention apart from machine intelligence.
